secondary_observations.what: A save and a reload buy back the night rate: 42 souls become 57 for the same enemy.
secondary_observations.detail: save/state.js:344-348 persists clock.time_of_day, clock.day_count and clock.weather. _awardFrames and awardTimeOfDay are in NEITHER the blob nor the loader. A load therefore writes env.timeOfDay from outside the step, Environment._syncFromFloat re-seats the award clock on it, and the death-stolen offset vanishes. Near the DAWN edge that offset runs against the player, so discharging it is a gain: from 04:48, 20 deaths leave the world clock at 4.802 and the award clock at 5.078, and one inf_trash pays 42; saving and reloading the same state re-seats the award clock to 4.802 and the same enemy pays 57. +35% for a reload, with no world event in between. It is invisible to m_d4_across_death_diff and m_d10_d11_preserved by construction, because they diff the save blob and the field is not in it. Remedy: put clock.award_frames in the blob and read it back — one field, one line each side, and m_d4 starts covering it for free.

secondary_observations.what: weather.json's state array order is load-bearing and nothing says so.
secondary_observations.detail: Environment._roll() walks m.states in array order accumulating `acc += w[i]` and returns the first id whose partial sum exceeds the draw. Re-running 40,000 f@60 with the state array reversed settles the world on `still` instead of `canopy_dim`. Not a defect today — the order comes from a JSON array — but the weather machine's determinism is a property of a data file's key order rather than of its arithmetic, and a future generator emitting states from an object or a Map would change the weather without changing a line of code. The clock beside it is immune by construction: it is an integer frame counter, and the accumulate-a-float clock it replaced drifts 9.578e-11 h per game day (measured). This is the same IEEE-754 family a sibling piece root-caused elsewhere, living in this very file and currently masked.

corpus_extended.what: Comparison method 8's four assertions are all READS OF A PROJECTION OF THE HOUR. 'merchants are closed' is settlement.js#isOpen(id, hour) and 'the night roster is active' is npc.js#slotAt(schedule, hour) — both pure functions of the clock, so the four-rest round-trip clause ('returns to the same shop state') cannot fail unless the clock arithmetic fails and carries no independent information. The one clause that drives a CONSUMER rather than reading a projection — an ordinary kill paying 1.35x after the rest, through sim/souls.js awardFor — is not in the item at all; the W1-13 round-3 verdict added it as acceptance and round 4 measured it. Proposed amendment: method 8 gains a fifth assertion, 'an ordinary enemy killed after the rest pays NIGHT_MULTIPLIER x what the same archetype paid before it, with a no-rest control at exactly 1.00', and its round-trip clause is either restated as a clock check or replaced by the rest-kill-rest observation (an ordinary respawns, a named one does not) that RI-PRG04 method 1 already owns. As written the method's strongest evidence lives only in a verdict and its weakest clause reads as a world observation.

arbitration_questions.question: Is it acceptable that the souls economy and the province can disagree about whether it is night — that after 22 deaths without resting an enemy pays the night rate while every shop in the world is still open — and if not, which of RI-PRG04 §6 rule 4 (the clock must not advance on death) and AR-1 (a death must not pay) gives way?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: AR-1 is absolute: spending N frames dead and N frames alive must leave the same enemy worth the same. That requires a clock that ticks through death, which is what the award clock is.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: RI-PRG04 §6 rule 4 is equally absolute: dying repeatedly at a boss must not burn a quest deadline. That requires a clock that does NOT tick through death. The world the player looks at — shops, schedules, the journal date — must be one clock, and a price that disagrees with the sky is a Morrowind-side incoherence.
arbitration_questions.why_it_cannot_be_settled_by_a_builder: The two requirements are jointly unsatisfiable with one clock, so the build's answer — two clocks, discharged at every rest — is the only shape that meets both, and the residual incoherence is a consequence rather than a defect. Whether that residual is acceptable, and up to what offset, is a design ruling and not a measurement. A third option exists and should be ruled on rather than assumed away: charge the death interval to the award clock ONLY, and let quest deadlines read a third quantity (days elapsed) that death cannot move either.
arbitration_questions.proposed_default: Accept the two clocks, bound the offset (discharge it at a ceiling as well as at a rest), publish award_offset_h as a scored quantity, and persist it in the save so a reload is neutral.

Round 4 ran RI-PRG04's Comparison method 8 for the first time in four rounds, and in doing so found an AR-1 leak its own predecessor had shipped — a world clock frozen by death, read by the souls economy, so that dying at the dawn edge paid 35 per cent more than living the same frames. Under ARBITRATION §3 that is an automatic fail of the piece regardless of score, and the round found it against itself, named it correctly, and closed it in four executable lines. I could not break the closure: a source-level deletion reproduces the defect exactly, a 2x2 shows both halves of the fix are individually necessary, the invariant holds at 96 of 96 start hours, and a reach census says neither clock touches a frame number, a damage value, a poise value or a stamina value anywhere in the build. What holds the piece at 6 is not that. It is that the one clause the previous verdict wrote an acceptance for — a named NPC in a different place after the rest, WITH THE REST REMOVED AS THE CONTROL — is scored against a control arm containing nobody, reports a Lilmoth roster taken from Archon's hearth, and comes back pass: false in the aggregation, which the builder disclosed and left open. The fix is excellent. The evidence for the number beside it is not.
